assessments.rationale: Python backend work (Django REST Framework APIs; Flask endpoints) is evidenced in two professional roles. Counting calendar duration with 'Present' read as the CV's June 2024 date: Example Logistics March 2022 – June 2024 (about 27–28 months) plus Example Pay Startup January 2021 – February 2022 (about 13–14 months, part-time, flagged) gives roughly 40–42 months, and at least about 38 months even on the most conservative reading of month boundaries; the periods do not overlap. The standard counts part-time professional work by calendar duration, so the 3-year minimum is met. The June–August 2020 internship (CSV data scripts, not backend) is excluded. Grade B because reaching the threshold depends on a part-time role.

positioning: Position Candidate A as a Python backend engineer with professional experience from January 2021 to June 2024 (the first role part-time) building REST APIs with Django REST Framework and Flask, designing PostgreSQL schemas and writing migrations, writing pytest unit tests, setting up a GitHub Actions CI workflow, deploying services to AWS EC2 via a scripted release process, adding structured JSON logging, and taking part in GitHub pull-request code review. Supporting points: helped onboard two interns, holds a BSc in Computer Science (2021), is based remotely in EMEA, and has used Celery, Redis and Docker Compose on a personal project. Do not claim API design ownership, query performance tuning, integration testing, operating cloud services, production containerisation, Kubernetes, Kafka, metrics/tracing, on-call experience or a completed AWS certification; mandatory gap: no evidence of on-call experience or availability (A1), which must be addressed directly.
application_brief: Candidate A is a remote, EMEA-based backend engineer working mainly in Python. At Example Logistics Ltd (March 2022 – present, CV dated June 2024) they built and maintained REST APIs with Django REST Framework for an internal shipment-tracking service used by three internal teams, designed PostgreSQL table schemas and migrations, wrote pytest unit tests for the API layer, set up a GitHub Actions workflow running the test suite on every pull request, deployed services to AWS EC2 using a scripted release process, added structured JSON logging, and took part in code review. Previously, in a part-time role (January 2021 – February 2022), they developed Flask endpoints, wrote MySQL reporting queries, reviewed code via GitHub pull requests and helped onboard two interns. They hold a BSc in Computer Science (2021); an AWS Cloud Practitioner certification is in progress. Points to verify: API design responsibility, query tuning, integration testing, operating services, Kubernetes, and on-call availability.
uncertainties: Mandatory gap: the CV contains no evidence of on-call experience or availability for the on-call rotation (A1).

M1 duration is computed from month-level dates with 'Present' read as June 2024 (CV last-updated date); it relies on a part-time role (January 2021 – February 2022) whose hours are not stated. The internship (June–August 2020) is excluded.

Responsibilities and the 'Location' line were judged to be explicit obligations/conditions; on-call (A1) and location (A2) were not labelled mandatory or preferred in the job description and were treated as mandatory per the standard's rule for ambiguous types.
'Significantly improved test coverage' is vague and was not credited as a metric.
Kubernetes, Kafka and Terraform appear only in the Skills list; Docker appears professionally nowhere and only locally in a personal project.
The AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner certification is in progress and was not treated as held.
The 'quarterly in-person team weeks' condition under 'What we offer' was not assessed as a requirement; the CV gives no information on travel availability.
